setlist_extra.title: Stuck Inside Of Mobile With The Memphis Blues Again

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Reviewer highlights a pair of Jacks in the first set, Jack Straw and Jack-A-Roe [18]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): Minglewood and Bird Song singled out as particularly sweet in a solid first set [20]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Reviewer danced hard during the jam out of Sugar Magnolia, calling it a fun set opener [16]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Sugar Magnolia into Scarlet Begonias transition is called seamless and possibly the best they ever played [17]
- **China Doll** (1 review): The end of China Doll is praised for Jerry's MIDI work [22]
- **The Mighty Quinn** (1 other source): Quinn the Eskimo was taped at the end of the first set on this source [8]
- **Memphis Blues** (1 review): Harmonies on the Memphis number are singled out as especially well oiled [15]

## Setlist highlights

- **The Memphis Blues Again**: rare: 13 archived performances [27]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-07-18.sbd.walstib.435.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 155 min; rated 3.75/5 by 12 [1]
- **gd1989-07-18.138496.ultra.matrix.sbd.miller.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 154 min [2]
- **gd89-07-18.sbd.9854.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 147 min; rated 4.68/5 by 37 [5]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the soundboard a nice recording of a sweet-sounding band, with Phil's bass deep in the mix; Reviewer calls the sound quality superb; Reviewer rates sound an A, noting the bass is a bit too high [15][20][24]
- **gd1989-07-18.mtx.hansokolow.96231.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 150 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [6]
- **gd1989-07-18.sbd.brantley.28474.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 147 min; rated 3.5/5 by 4 [7]
- **gd1989-07-18.senn441.coniff.gmb.92430.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 146 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [8]

## Around the show

- Reviewer sneaked toward the stage between sets into an area roped off with police tape, and nobody objected [16]
- Reviewer says this opened a four-show run at the venue, with cooler weather than the previous year [18]
- A commenter says they got puddled on during Drums at the show [29]
- Sugar Magnolia into Scarlet is rated equal to the same pairing at Buffalo in 1990 [18]
- Reviewer prefers the Sugar into Scarlet combination from 3/27/88, which jams Sugar longer and goes into Fire [20]
- Reviewer ranks this three-night run among the best post-coma Dead shows and wishes all nights were on the DVD [25]
- Reviewer's favorite of the three nights because of the adventurous setlist, including Sugar, Scarlet and Smarter [26]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-07-18.sbd.walstib.435.shnf**: transferred by Nick Georges; source: DSBD>DAT>CD [1]
- **gd1989-07-18.138496.ultra.matrix.sbd.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Ultra Matrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) [2]. Also: Two sets of master tapes were combined to complete the show; a 24-bit transfer was converted to 16-bit [2]
- **gd89-07-18.sbd.9854.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jason Brantley; source: DSBD [5]
- **gd1989-07-18.mtx.hansokolow.96231.flac16**: transferred by hansokolow; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [6]. Also: Matrix mixed by hansokolow in ProTools from a soundboard and an audience tape by Casey Coniff; Audience source: Sennheiser 441 into Marantz PDM 340 with dbx, recorded in front of repeater stack onto Maxell cassette [6]
- **gd1989-07-18.sbd.brantley.28474.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jason Brantley; source: DSBD [7]. Also: Soundboard transfer by Brantley; a sector boundary error in disc one track two was fixed by William at TuneTree [7]
- **gd1989-07-18.senn441.coniff.gmb.92430.flac16**: taped by Casey Coniff; transferred by Bill Koucky; source: Sennheiser 441 > Marantz PDM 340 w/ dbx (Cassette Master Maxell MX-S 90) [8]. Also: Crossfades cover tape flips after Friend of the Devil, during Drums and before the encore; no patch sources used [8]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Alpine Valley Music Theatre - July 18, 1989](https://www.dead.net/show/july-18-1989) [28]
- Fan art by www.tbanjo.com: [Grateful Dead Go to the Movies: Alpine Valley, 7/18/89](http://www.tbanjo.com/2012/04/grateful-dead-go-to-movies-alpine.html) [31]
- Poster by Carlos Pérez Báez: [Grateful Dead estrena la película del concierto de 1989 en el "Alpine Valley Music Theatre" de Wisconsin - Dirty Rock Ma](https://www.dirtyrock.info/2012/03/grateful-dead-estrena-la-pelicula-del-concierto-de-1989-en-el-alpine-valley-music-theatre-de-wisconsin/) [32]
- Poster by Robbi Cohn: [1989-07-18 Alpine Valley Music Theatre, East Troy, WI, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1989-07-18-alpine-valley-music-theatre-east-troy-wi-usa/) [33]

claims.text: Harmonies on the Memphis number are singled out as especially well oiled
Reviewer calls the soundboard a nice recording of a sweet-sounding band, with Phil's bass deep in the mix
Reviewer sneaked toward the stage between sets into an area roped off with police tape, and nobody objected
Reviewer danced hard during the jam out of Sugar Magnolia, calling it a fun set opener
Sugar Magnolia into Scarlet Begonias transition is called seamless and possibly the best they ever played
Reviewer says this opened a four-show run at the venue, with cooler weather than the previous year
Sugar Magnolia into Scarlet is rated equal to the same pairing at Buffalo in 1990
Reviewer highlights a pair of Jacks in the first set, Jack Straw and Jack-A-Roe
Reviewer prefers the Sugar into Scarlet combination from 3/27/88, which jams Sugar longer and goes into Fire
Minglewood and Bird Song singled out as particularly sweet in a solid first set
Reviewer calls the sound quality superb
The end of China Doll is praised for Jerry's MIDI work
Reviewer rates sound an A, noting the bass is a bit too high
Reviewer ranks this three-night run among the best post-coma Dead shows and wishes all nights were on the DVD
Reviewer's favorite of the three nights because of the adventurous setlist, including Sugar, Scarlet and Smarter
Two sets of master tapes were combined to complete the show; a 24-bit transfer was converted to 16-bit
Matrix mixed by hansokolow in ProTools from a soundboard and an audience tape by Casey Coniff
Audience source: Sennheiser 441 into Marantz PDM 340 with dbx, recorded in front of repeater stack onto Maxell cassette
Soundboard transfer by Brantley; a sector boundary error in disc one track two was fixed by William at TuneTree
Crossfades cover tape flips after Friend of the Devil, during Drums and before the encore; no patch sources used
Quinn the Eskimo was taped at the end of the first set on this source
A commenter says they got puddled on during Drums at the show
